Recent work also combines neural perception with a non-neural crossing predictor. PCAP-SL uses frozen vision-transformer features from pedestrian crops, OpenPose coordinates, and ego-speed where available, with a sequence of XGBoost classifiers carrying prediction information across observation steps \cite{Benkabou2026PCAPSL}. Here XGBoost is a learned ensemble of decision trees; a fixed feature-extraction procedure does not make the crossing decision a hand-written rule. PCAP-SL is relevant to the architecture studied in this thesis because it separates upstream neural feature extraction from downstream tree-based prediction. Its crop embeddings and sequential learning procedure differ from the proposed pose-derived architecture defined in Chapter~\ref{chap:methodology}. Efficiency comparisons must specify whether they include upstream perception or only the crossing predictor.

For the present thesis, vision--language approaches are therefore relevant as an adjacent interpretability direction rather than as a direct experimental baseline. Discriminative variants such as ClipCross learn language-aligned semantic features, whereas generative variants can expose decisions through natural-language responses. The narrower question pursued here is whether part of the evidence supplied to a classifier can itself consist of named, fixed, and inspectable geometric measurements. The conceptual foundations of that representation are discussed below; its equations are defined in Chapter~\ref{chap:methodology}.
